gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each 3-channel camera costs once the maker's own parking-mode hardwire kit and a card are added: the Vantrue N4 Pro S passes $300 with the kit alone ($309.98), the N4S stays under with the kit ($229.98) and a 64 GB card ($272.97), and no candidate stays under $300 with a 256 GB card (Vantrue's own N4S + kit + 256 GB bundle is $314.99).
standout_why: Compared against productbible.com/blog/best-3-channel-dash-cams, the only rival page that opened. It gives camera prices and per-channel resolution and says 'At least 256GB for daily driving', but has no hardwire-kit price, no card price and no all-in total. ChatGPT's own answer asks 'Does $300 include accessories?' and never prices them. vortexradar.com/best-dashcams returned 403 and ezdashcam.com/collections/under-300 returned 429, so neither cited page was compared; the 3 rests on Product Bible and the ChatGPT answer text alone.
decides: If $300 is for the camera alone, the Vantrue N4 Pro S ($279.99, a product we link) fits, but the $20.01 left is less than the $29.99 kit that names it, so parking mode takes it to $309.98. If $300 must cover parking mode, the Vantrue N4S wins: $229.98 with the kit, $272.97 with Vantrue's 64 GB card added. With a 256 GB card ($119.99 at Vantrue, $149.82 for Samsung PRO Endurance on Amazon) nothing here stays under $300, so ChatGPT's line that the N4S leaves room for 'a high-endurance microSD card and hardwire kit' holds only for a small card. The N4S also costs least per recorded megapixel ($16.11 against $19.92 for the N4 Pro S).
